name: secretsmanager:PutSecretValue on arn:aws:secretsmanager:us-east-1:123456789012:secret:app/* (one account) is NOT broad
note: S1-dataexfil-arn iteration 4 over-correction guard for the account-wildcard fix. The must-warn sibling pins account='*' (arn:aws:secretsmanager:*:*:secret:app/*) and MUST fire WILDCARD-RESOURCE; this pins a CONCRETE account (123456789012) and region, scoping the app/ secret path to ONE account. Making a leading-wildcard ACCOUNT broad must NOT start flagging a concrete-account secret-path prefix. Only the trailing key under app/ is wildcarded, so the grant stays account-scoped. The engine MUST NOT emit WILDCARD-RESOURCE here.
rationale: arn:aws:secretsmanager:us-east-1:123456789012:secret:app/* names secrets under the 'app/' path in ONE concrete account (123456789012) and region - a bounded, path-prefixed subset, not every secret across every account. The account segment is a concrete 12-digit id, not '*'/'?', so the grant does not cross the account boundary; only the key under app/ is wildcarded. isBroadArnResource treats a leading-wildcard ACCOUNT as broad but a concrete account keeps it single-account, so a trailing path wildcard behind it stays quiet - materially narrower than the all-accounts arn:aws:secretsmanager:*:*:secret:app/* the must-warn corpus locks. Ref: AWS ARN account-id segment; Secrets Manager path scoping.
